The Chinese false gudgeon Abbottina rivularis is a small-bodied cyprinid inhabiting slow-flowing freshwater systems across East Asia. Field surveys indicate that this species attains a maximum recorded total length of 18.9 cm [Li = 18.9 cm], a size that is modest compared to many of its cyprinid relatives. Reproductively active females captured in the Yangtze River basin during the spawning season exhibited a wet weight at the onset of puberty of 0.87 grams [Wwp = 0.87 grams], a value that reflects the relatively small body size at which gonadal maturation begins. The incubation period of the demersal, adhesive eggs has been studied under controlled laboratory conditions. At a stable water temperature of 18 °C [T = 18 °C], the mean duration from fertilisation to chorion rupture, i.e., the age at birth, was recorded as 15 days [ab = 15 days]. This comparatively short embryonic phase is typical of many small cyprinids that spawn in warm, productive waters where rapid development may enhance larval survival by reducing the window of vulnerability to benthic predators.

Data on lifetime reproductive output in A. rivularis have been compiled from multiple field studies. Under thermal conditions of 18 °C [T = 18 °C], females typically construct nests and deposit approximately 1711 eggs per nest [N_R_i = approximately 1711 eggs per nest], a fecundity that is considerable given the modest adult body size. The same individuals are capable of completing about 2 nesting events per year [F_R_i = about 2 nesting events per year] during the protracted spawning season, resulting in a daily reproduction rate of approximately 9.37 eggs per day [Ri = approximately 9.37 eggs per day]. The wet weight of newly hatched yolk-sac larvae is remarkably low; upon eclosion, the wet weight at birth is estimated at 0.00052 grams [Wwb = 0.00052 grams], a value that underscores the species' reliance on small, energy-rich endogenous yolk reserves to sustain the non-feeding prolarva through the first few days of development.

Growth trajectories derived from scale annuli and length-frequency histograms show that A. rivularis reaches puberty, defined by the onset of vitellogenesis in females and spermiation in males, when individuals attain a total length of 4.5 cm [Lp = 4.5 cm]. This threshold is typically crossed during the second growing season, after which individuals enter the reproductively active adult phase. The ultimate wet weight, representing the asymptotic body mass attained by fully grown adults, has been estimated at 79 grams [Wwi = 79 grams] based on length-weight regressions fitted to a large sample of individuals spanning the full size range. This allometric relationship predicts that the heaviest specimens, approaching the maximum total length of 18.9 cm, will reach roughly 79 grams, a mass that is consistent with the modest energetic demands of a benthic invertebrate feeder in temperate lotic habitats.

Longevity data for A. rivularis have been obtained from mark-recapture studies conducted over a decade in a stable stream reach. At the typical thermal regime of the study site (18 °C [T = 18 °C]), the maximum lifespan recorded among tagged individuals was 4 years [am = 4 years]. This relatively short lifespan, characteristic of many small-bodied cyprinids with early maturation and high reproductive effort, positions the species as an opportunistic life-history strategist. In comparison with congeneric species such as Abbottina springeri, which occasionally lives beyond five years, the four-year maximum lifespan of A. rivularis may reflect a trade-off between early and intense reproduction and somatic persistence. The life cycle thus spans a brief four-year window, with most mortality concentrated in the post-spawning period as individuals approach senescence.

Comparative ecophysiology further illuminates the adaptive context of A. rivularis life-history traits. At 18 °C [T = 18 °C], the embryonic duration of 15 days [ab = 15 days] places the species mid-range among temperate cyprinids; for example, the common gudgeon Gobio gobio requires a similar incubation period under analogous thermal conditions. The egg mass of 0.00052 grams, which corresponds to the wet weight of the egg shortly before hatching, aligns well with the egg diameters typical of the Gobioninae subfamily. Furthermore, the total length at puberty of 4.5 cm [Lp = 4.5 cm] represents approximately 24% of the ultimate total length of 18.9 cm [Li = 18.9 cm], a ratio that is consistent with an early-maturing, high-fecundity life cycle adapted to variable, disturbance-prone environments where rapid population turnover confers a selective advantage.
